item.title: [Feature] Option to fade the first notch too, so slow scrolling feels like the direct IKEA binding
item.body:
> **AI disclosure.** The observations below are from my own setup; the text was drafted with an AI assistant (Claude Code) and checked by me.

**Setup:** v0.6.1 · HA 2026.11.1 (HAOS) · BILRESA scroll wheel (E2490) over Thread, firmware 1.9.15 · targets are 4 single IKEA KAJPLATS bulbs over Matter/Thread (firmware 1.2.0) · brightness mode, step 5, perceptual curve, transition 0.5

**What I see**

When the wheel is paired directly with the bulbs (IKEA's own Matter binding), every notch fades smoothly, including the very first one and including slow, one-notch-at-a-time turning. That is simply the **default behaviour of the direct pairing**, with nothing to configure. It is what people expect from this wheel, because that is how it behaves out of the box.

Through a binding of this integration, the same slow turning makes each notch land as a visible jump. My family found the binding version noticeably less smooth than the direct pairing, so I removed the bindings.

I understand from `_smoothing_transition()` and #31 / #14 that this is on purpose: the first batch of a scroll is never faded so the first notch reacts at once, and in the 0.7 line every later batch of the same scroll gets the full transition. With slow, deliberate turning, though, almost every notch starts a new scroll and is a single-notch first batch, so it always gets transition 0.

**What works for me now**

An automation on the channel events instead of a binding: 5 % per notch, **0.4 s transition on every notch, including the first**, `mode: queued`. It still feels immediate (the fade starts at once, it just doesn't snap), and in a direct comparison it is very close to the IKEA direct binding. Longer transitions (1.0–1.5 s) and acceleration felt worse, so the sweet spot seems to be a short fade rather than none.

**Request**

Fade the first notch too, so a binding behaves like the direct pairing by default. Since the direct pairing does exactly this out of the box, I'd suggest it as the **default**, with an option to turn it off for anyone who prefers the instant snap (for example **"Fade the first notch"**, on by default, or a separate *first-notch transition* in seconds). A short fade still starts immediately, so the eager first reaction is kept; it just doesn't snap.

Related: #9 (point 2) asked for something similar for Zigbee2MQTT groups; this request is only about the first notch with single bulbs.

Thanks for the integration and the careful work on the scroll timing!
